candidates.rule: The seller’s price floor is the higher of 72% of list price and 1.12 times cost, so every completed deal preserves at least 12% over cost.
candidates.quote: floor 72% and cost x 1.12 unchanged
candidates.harness: Reject or counter offers below the higher floor.

candidates.rule: The seller accepts offers at or above its floor starting on turn 2; its opening ask is 74% of list price.
candidates.quote: opens at 74% of list
candidates.harness: Use a 74%-of-list opening and permit floor-level acceptance from turn 2.

candidates.rule: In the last hour before 06:06 on 2026-11-04, 30 deals closed at a median 76% of list and 29.5% over cost; 31 real buyers left after a 78% opening, while 23 cancellations were quote-only surveys.
candidates.quote: 30 sold at a median 76% of list, 29.5% over cost
candidates.harness: Track completed deals separately from quote-only cancellations and monitor exits at the opening price.

candidates.rule: Night mode gives deeper stock to best-selling items and caps the line allocation at 0.6.
candidates.quote: best sellers deeper, line cap 0.6
candidates.harness: Apply the night-mode stock allocation when night mode is active.

candidates.rule: At 08:35 on 2026-11-04, shop ALL was 0.613 with 2,164,095 profit, 34,983,436 revenue, 252 deals and 4.52 stars; buyer surplus was 2,828,339 over 327 deals and 114 posts, and player percentile was 52.1 with player score 0.993.
candidates.quote: player 0.993 (percentile 52.1)
candidates.harness: Record shop ALL, buyer results and player percentile together when evaluating performance.

candidates.rule: Collect seller negotiations, buyer orders and payments, restock windows, model timeouts and tool refusals over the preceding 30 minutes every five minutes; alert at most once per hour per crossed threshold and include the snapshot in the strategy brief.
candidates.quote: every 5 min over the last 30 min
candidates.harness: Run the health checks on that cadence, rate-limit threshold alerts, and pass snapshots to the strategy brief.

candidates.rule: The first health snapshot on 2026-11-04 around 08:5x showed 48 settled and 48 left at the opening out of 129 visits, 27 no-stock visits, and 36 paid versus 14 unpaid buyer orders; 11 unpaid orders were short of shelf life.
candidates.quote: 48 settled and 48 left at the opening of 129 visits
candidates.harness: Expose these counts and unpaid-order reasons in health reporting.

candidates.rule: Counting buyer payments only since the previous health run caused a false “paid nothing” alert; payment status must be evaluated with correct timing and across the intended observation window.
candidates.quote: counted payments since the last run and raised a false 'paid nothing' alert
candidates.harness: Test payment-window accounting and suppress alerts based on an incorrect run-to-run count.

candidates.rule: Restart the seller and outer harness after a schema change so both use the new schema.
candidates.quote: seller and outer restarted for the schema
candidates.harness: Restart affected processes after schema changes.

candidates.rule: On 2026-11-04 around 10:3x, the user chose to let the top three goods SKUs by expected sales value hold up to 20 units and consume 50% of the window’s money, while other SKUs remain capped at 12 units.
candidates.quote: the top 3 goods SKUs by expected sales value may hold 20 units and take 50% of the window's money
candidates.harness: Apply the top-three stock and budget shares while retaining the 12-unit cap for other lines.

candidates.rule: Record goods orders the shop cannot serve, including category, budget and accepted SKUs; during restocking, for each recorded order in the last six hours, stock two units of the best-selling accepted market SKU that fits the budget at 75% of list.
candidates.quote: the accepted SKU that sells most in the market and fits the budget at 75% of list (2 units)
candidates.harness: Save unserved-order demand and use it in the next restock decision.

candidates.rule: The buyer cannot buy from its own shop, supply opens every 20 minutes, and the kit accepts another order only after the buyer ends; it cannot wait within an order for a shop to restock.
candidates.quote: the kit takes the next order only after the buyer ends, and supply opens every 20 min
candidates.harness: Do not plan on the buyer purchasing its own seller’s stock or waiting inside an order for restock.

candidates.rule: On 2026-11-04 around 10:4x, the user wanted the buyer to visit many shops quickly and not squeeze food sellers on price.
candidates.quote: visit many shops fast, do not squeeze food
candidates.harness: Prioritize quick shop visits and avoid aggressive food-price bargaining.

candidates.rule: The next buyer order arrived about 20 seconds after the buyer ended an order: median 20.4 seconds across 92 orders.
candidates.quote: median 20.4 s over 92 orders
candidates.harness: Do not assume that finishing substantially faster than 20 seconds yields another order sooner.

candidates.rule: Buyer shop-search time budgets are 20 seconds and at most eight shops for food, and 120 seconds and at most ten shops for goods; wait up to eight seconds for a food shop message and 20 seconds for a goods shop message, including card fetches.
candidates.quote: food 20 s, up to 8 shops; goods 120 s, up to 10
candidates.harness: Enforce the per-category time, shop-count and response-wait limits.

candidates.rule: Food offers open at 55% of list, aim for 70% of list, and retain an 80% ceiling.
candidates.quote: food opens at 55% and aims at 70% of list with the 80% ceiling kept
candidates.harness: Use the stated food opening, target and ceiling.

candidates.rule: In the reported food negotiations, 37 of 84 completed, 35 were refused at the first message and seven buyers walked.
candidates.quote: food: 37 of 84 completed, 35 refused at the first message, 7 walked
candidates.harness: Track food completion, first-message refusals and walkaways separately.

candidates.rule: Board percentiles use only buyers with a deal (44 of 119) and shops with a deal or purchase (47 of 80); missing values count as zero and ties receive half credit.
candidates.harness: Compute percentiles using the board’s eligible pools, treating missing values as zero and ties as half.

candidates.rule: On 2026-11-04, corrected buyer percentiles were surplus 28.4, forum 53.4, deals 37.5 and posts 83.0; surplus, weighted 0.5, was the weakest buyer metric, not forum.
candidates.quote: surplus 28.4 (we read 73.7), forum 53.4, deals 37.5, posts 83.0
candidates.harness: Use corrected board-pool percentiles and prioritize buyer surplus rather than forum rating.

candidates.rule: The corrected seller stars percentile was 34.0 on 2026-11-04; the earlier overnight report’s weakest-metric diagnosis was corrected because its buyer surplus percentile was misread.
candidates.quote: shop stars 34.0
candidates.harness: Recalculate seller and buyer percentiles from the board’s eligible pools before diagnosing weak metrics.

candidates.rule: The harness must report health metrics, feed exceptions back into operations, restart automatically on schema changes, log on start and address flaky index tests; these were listed as next harness needs in the 2026-11-04 overnight report.
candidates.quote: health metrics in outer/watch, exception feedback, auto-restart on schema change
candidates.harness: Implement the listed monitoring, feedback, restart, startup logging and test-reliability behaviors.
